claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase alloy.
TC4 has low hardness and limited friction and wear resistance under extreme-service or high-contact-stress conditions.
HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for use as a coating on TC4.
The proposed intervention is cold-spray deposition at particle velocities of approximately 300–400 m/s while maintaining the substrate below 200 degrees Celsius.
The proposed post-deposition treatment is an inert-atmosphere anneal at approximately 700 degrees Celsius for one hour.
Cold spraying will consolidate the HfNbTaTiZr particles onto TC4 with minimal thermal input.
The limited thermal input during cold spraying will prevent unwanted phase transformations in TC4.
The anneal will induce controlled interdiffusion between the HfNbTaTiZr coating and the TC4 substrate.
Controlled interdiffusion will produce a graded interface with metallurgical bonding and compositional homogeneity.
The graded interface will reduce residual stresses.
The selected annealing treatment will avoid deleterious intermetallic-compound formation.
The coating and graded interface will significantly increase surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The coating and graded interface will improve friction and wear resistance relative to untreated TC4 under extreme-service conditions.
The intervention will preserve the ductility and advantageous bulk properties of the TC4 substrate.
Annealing parameters can be optimized to obtain effective interdiffusion without compromising the TC4 microstructure.
